17 spots in NYC to watch the U.S. Open and sip a Honey Deuce
The U.S. Open is set to return to Queens’ Billie Jean King National Tennis Center for another year of world-class competition. As the world’s best tennis players battle for the final Grand Slam titles of the year, the tournament will once again bring plenty of excitement to the five boroughs, along with one of its most iconic drinks: the Honey Deuce. Ahead, we’ve found some of the best spots in NYC to watch the U.S. Open while enjoying a Honey Deuce cocktail.
Backyard at Hudson Yards
A jam-packed U.S. Open schedule returns to one of the city’s most iconic public spaces, transforming Hudson Yards into a tennis fan hub. The free, weeklong activation runs from Sunday, August 30, through Saturday, September 5, from 11 a.m. to 8 p.m., with watch parties, tennis-themed video games, two 40-foot sport courts, and Honey Deuce cocktails. Fans can also experience what it’s like to walk through the player tunnel into Arthur Ashe Stadium, browse official tournament merchandise, and enjoy live DJ sets throughout the week.
Edge
30 Hudson Yards, Hudson Yards
Edge, the highest sky deck in the Western Hemisphere, is taking the tennis-viewing experience to new heights. The observation deck will screen matches live 100 stories above Manhattan, providing a one-of-a-kind setting to watch the tournament. Visitors can sip Honey Deuces while taking in the action from high above the city.
Magic Hour Rooftop
Moxy Times Square, 485 7th Avenue, Midtown
Magic Hour Rooftop, perched above Moxy Times Square, is serving Honey Deuces and streaming the tournament on 10 giant TVs across its indoor and outdoor spaces. Patrons can watch the U.S. Open while taking in scenic views of the Empire State Building and surrounding skyline. The cocktails will be served in souvenir cups, alongside a sparkling Paloma and glasses of Moët Imperial Brut, according to Time Out.
Lydia’s
161 1st Avenue, East Village
The East Village social sports club Lydia’s is screening the U.S. Open on several large screens, allowing visitors to take in the action with a Honey Deuce in hand. Patrons can enjoy the signature cocktail for $13, as well as beer bucket specials, throughout the tournament.
The Wolfe
425 Amsterdam Avenue, Upper West Side
Named after acclaimed novelist and longtime New Yorker Tom Wolfe, this Upper West Side sports bar is offering several special menu items for the U.S. Open. At The Wolfe, patrons can enjoy tournament staples like chicken nuggets with caviar and Honey Deuces served in special cups throughout the Open.
Stout NYC
Four locations across Manhattan
Stout will serve Honey Deuce cocktails at all four of its Manhattan locations throughout the tournament, offering tennis fans a lively place to enjoy the festive drink. The bar has outposts in Midtown West, Midtown East, the Financial District, and near Bryant Park.
Arlo Hotels
Nomad and Williamsburg
Two Arlo Hotels locations in Nomad and Williamsburg are hosting official U.S. Open watch parties and pop-ups in partnership with Grey Goose. On September 2, ART NoMad at 11 East 31st Street and Sungold at Arlo Williamsburg at 96 Wythe Avenue will from 4 p.m. to 6 p.m. offer sweeping city views, Grey Goose giveaways, and complimentary samples of Honey Deuce cocktails on a first-come, first-served basis.
Industry Kitchen
70 South Street, South Street Seaport
Enjoy refreshing cocktails and savory fare just steps from the waterfront at the Seaport’s Industry Kitchen. The 5,000-square-foot restaurant and event space is offering a special U.S. Open “courtside menu” throughout the tournament, featuring tennis-themed dishes like “center court tuna tacos,” “the Open burger,” and “Match Point Surf & Turf.” The menu will be available through September 13.
The Standard Biergarten
848 Washington Street, High Line, Meatpacking District
Don’t miss a single serve at the High Line’s Standard Biergarten this U.S. Open, where live matches will be shown through September 13. The vibrant venue will offer a selection of themed cocktails, including the Honey Deuce, an Ace Paloma made with Dobel Cristalino tequila, grapefruit soda, and black lava salt, and a non-alcoholic “Love All” made with Seedlip, lemongrass, lavender, lime, and soda.
Recreation Bar
Moxy NYC Downtown, 26 Ann Street, Financial District
The old-school Recreation Bar inside Moxy NYC Downtown is screening the matches and offering all-day cocktail specials in partnership with Grey Goose throughout the tournament. Patrons can enjoy $18 U.S. Open-themed cocktails, including the Honey Deuce, a Patron Paloma made with Patrón Silver, grapefruit soda, fresh lime, and salt, and a Berry Rouge Royale made with Grey Goose Berry Rouge, lemonade, brut rosé, and soda water.
Gibney’s NYC
228 West 39th Street, Midtown
Gibney’s NY is inviting tennis enthusiasts to sip festive cocktails while catching all of the U.S. Open action across its three floors and rooftop. Patrons can enjoy Honey Deuces, along with a selection of creative cocktails, including several options that honor the venue’s Irish roots. They can also get into the racket spirit with a game of table tennis, allowing them to sip and serve between matches.
Broken Shaker NY
Freehand Hotel, 23 Lexington Avenue, 8th Floor, Flatiron
Flatiron’s boutique Freehand NY Hotel is turning its tranquil wraparound indoor-outdoor rooftop into a U.S. Open hub. During the tournament, the destination is serving Honey Deuces alongside Ace Palomas. Guests can enjoy the signature cocktails while watching U.S. Open matches during the bar’s business hours, with stunning skyline views as a backdrop.
Red Rooster Harlem
310 Lenox Avenue, Harlem
Harlem’s popular restaurant and live music venue Red Rooster is hosting daily U.S. Open watch parties and partnering with Grey Goose to offer official Honey Deuce cocktails throughout the tournament. Patrons can also enjoy a signature Maestro Dobel Ace Paloma made with Maestro Dobel tequila, grapefruit, agave, and fresh lime. Drink purchases will also go to a good cause, with Red Rooster donating 5 percent of proceeds from its featured U.S. Open cocktails to the Harlem Junior Tennis & Education Program, which gives young people access to tennis, education, and mentorship.
SUMMIT One Vanderbilt
45 East 42nd Street, Midtown East
Experience the U.S. Open more than 1,100 feet above Manhattan this tournament season. Summit One Vanderbilt’s sky-high cafe and terrace, Après, is serving Honey Deuces and screening every match, giving patrons a chance to enjoy the tournament with unparalleled views.
Tipsy NoMad
37 East 28th Street, Nomad
U.S. Open excitement comes with delicious food, signature cocktails, drink specials, and an energetic atmosphere at Tipsy NoMad. The bar is hosting match watch parties throughout the day through September 13, giving tennis fans a lively spot to catch the tournament in the neighborhood.
Beckett’s Sports Bar
81 Pearl Street, 48 Stone Street, Financial District
The Financial District’s longtime sports hub Beckett’s has gone into full U.S. Open mode. The sports bar is a great place to catch every serve and point while enjoying Honey Deuces and a wide variety of creative cocktails, starting at $16.
The William Vale
Westlight Rooftop, 111 North 12th Street, Williamsburg
The Westlight Rooftop, perched atop the William Vale hotel, is hosting a special U.S. Open-themed edition of its Sunset Sounds series. The Williamsburg celebration, presented by Grey Goose, will feature match screenings, ping pong tournaments, live DJ sets, and Honey Deuce cocktails. Tickets for the 21+ event cost $35 and can be purchased here.
